PBMC3k: an scRNA-seq lesson in R

This lesson executes the same R functions as the one-command workflow. Start from the project root. Its outputs are isolated in results/notebook_demo/. The dataset has one healthy donor; all automatic annotations remain candidates.

source("scripts/bootstrap.R")
check_packages()
cfg <- load_config("config/config.R")
cfg$output_dir <- "results/notebook_demo"
ensure_output(cfg)
## [1] "results/notebook_demo"
set.seed(cfg$seed)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, warning = TRUE)

1. Import raw counts

A count matrix contains integer UMI observations. Genes are rows and cells are columns in Seurat. The demo verifies the bundled checksums before importing.

stage_ingest(cfg)
## [1] "results/notebook_demo/objects/01_counts.rds"  
## [2] "results/notebook_demo/tables/gene_mapping.csv"
## [3] "results/notebook_demo/tables/samples.csv"     
## [4] "results/notebook_demo/provenance/inputs.json"
pbmc <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "ingest"))
dim(pbmc)
## [1] 32738  2700
sum(raw_counts(pbmc))
## [1] 6390631
head(pbmc[[]])
##                          orig.ident nCount_RNA nFeature_RNA sample_id  donor
## pbmc3k__AAACATACAACCAC-1     pbmc3k       2421          781    pbmc3k donor1
## pbmc3k__AAACATTGAGCTAC-1     pbmc3k       4903         1352    pbmc3k donor1
## pbmc3k__AAACATTGATCAGC-1     pbmc3k       3149         1131    pbmc3k donor1
## pbmc3k__AAACCGTGCTTCCG-1     pbmc3k       2639          960    pbmc3k donor1
## pbmc3k__AAACCGTGTATGCG-1     pbmc3k        981          522    pbmc3k donor1
## pbmc3k__AAACGCACTGGTAC-1     pbmc3k       2164          782    pbmc3k donor1
##                          condition  batch original_barcode
## pbmc3k__AAACATACAACCAC-1   healthy batch1 AAACATACAACCAC-1
## pbmc3k__AAACATTGAGCTAC-1   healthy batch1 AAACATTGAGCTAC-1
## pbmc3k__AAACATTGATCAGC-1   healthy batch1 AAACATTGATCAGC-1
## pbmc3k__AAACCGTGCTTCCG-1   healthy batch1 AAACCGTGCTTCCG-1
## pbmc3k__AAACCGTGTATGCG-1   healthy batch1 AAACCGTGTATGCG-1
## pbmc3k__AAACGCACTGGTAC-1   healthy batch1 AAACGCACTGGTAC-1

Question: Why must normalized values not be supplied as raw counts?

2. Quality control and doublets

The pipeline applies a minimum-gene screen, predicts doublets separately within the capture, then applies the remaining QC thresholds. Each cell receives an audit row. A high score is a prediction, not proof of a doublet.

stage_qc(cfg)
## [1] "results/notebook_demo/objects/02_qc.rds"    
## [2] "results/notebook_demo/tables/cell_qc.csv"   
## [3] "results/notebook_demo/tables/qc_summary.csv"
## [4] "results/notebook_demo/figures/qc.png"       
## [5] "results/notebook_demo/figures/doublets.png"
audit <- read.csv(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "tables/cell_qc.csv"))
table(audit$qc_keep)
## 
## FALSE  TRUE 
##   158  2542
sort(table(audit$removal_reason), decreasing = TRUE)
## 
##           retained  predicted_doublet high_mitochondrial         high_genes 
##               2542                 96                 57                  5
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "figures/qc.png")), rel_path = FALSE)

Question: How could strict mitochondrial filtering remove a real cell state?

3. Normalize and find variable genes

LogNormalize divides by the cell’s library size, scales to 10,000 and applies log1p. VST identifies variable genes. Scaling is restricted to variable features. The raw RNA count layer remains unchanged.

stage_normalize(cfg)
## [1] "results/notebook_demo/objects/03_normalized.rds" 
## [2] "results/notebook_demo/tables/variable_genes.csv" 
## [3] "results/notebook_demo/figures/variable_genes.png"
pbmc <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "normalize"))
head(SeuratObject::VariableFeatures(pbmc))
## [1] "PPBP"   "LYZ"    "S100A9" "FTL"    "IGLL5"  "GNLY"
SeuratObject::Layers(pbmc[["RNA"]])
## [1] "counts"     "data"       "scale.data"

Question: Why retain raw counts after creating normalized values?

4. PCA, graph clustering and UMAP

PCA summarizes scaled expression. Neighbors and Louvain clustering define groups. UMAP uses the R uwot implementation and visualizes local relationships.

stage_reduce(cfg)
## Warning: The default method for RunUMAP has changed from calling Python UMAP via reticulate to the R-native UWOT using the cosine metric
## To use Python UMAP via reticulate, set umap.method to 'umap-learn' and metric to 'correlation'
## This message will be shown once per session
## [1] "results/notebook_demo/objects/04_clustered.rds"   
## [2] "results/notebook_demo/tables/cluster_counts.csv"  
## [3] "results/notebook_demo/tables/umap_coordinates.csv"
## [4] "results/notebook_demo/figures/pca_elbow.png"      
## [5] "results/notebook_demo/figures/umap_clusters.png"
pbmc <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "reduce"))
Seurat::ElbowPlot(pbmc)

Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc, group.by = "cluster", label = TRUE)

Question: How might PCA dimension choice and clustering resolution alter the groups? Does a gap in UMAP prove a distinct biological lineage?

5. Find cluster markers

Wilcoxon tests compare each cluster to the other cells. Positive marker selection follows testing. Seurat’s adjusted marker p-values use Bonferroni correction. These exploratory comparisons are not donor-level disease tests.

stage_markers(cfg)
## [1] "results/notebook_demo/objects/05_markers.rds"      
## [2] "results/notebook_demo/objects/marker_universes.rds"
## [3] "results/notebook_demo/tables/markers_all.csv"      
## [4] "results/notebook_demo/tables/markers_positive.csv" 
## [5] "results/notebook_demo/tables/markers_top10.csv"    
## [6] "results/notebook_demo/tables/marker_test_audit.csv"
## [7] "results/notebook_demo/figures/marker_dotplot.png"  
## [8] "results/notebook_demo/figures/feature_markers.png"
markers <- read.csv(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "tables/markers_top10.csv"))
knitr::kable(head(markers, 15), digits = 3)

0 2.643 0.482 0.099 0 CCR7 0
0 2.627 0.127 0.028 0 SCGB3A1 0

knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "figures/marker_dotplot.png")), rel_path = FALSE)

Question: Why is one marker insufficient to label every cluster?

6. Review candidate annotations

Panel scores are heuristics. Inspect multiple lineage markers and conflicting evidence. NKG7 and PRF1 can appear in cytotoxic T cells as well as NK cells. Candidate T/NK labels therefore also consider CD3D, CD3E, TRAC, GNLY and KLRD1.

stage_annotate(cfg)
## [1] "results/notebook_demo/objects/06_annotated.rds"         
## [2] "results/notebook_demo/tables/annotation_evidence.csv"   
## [3] "results/notebook_demo/tables/annotation_scores.csv"     
## [4] "results/notebook_demo/tables/annotation_expression.csv" 
## [5] "results/notebook_demo/tables/celltype_counts.csv"       
## [6] "results/notebook_demo/tables/manual_labels_template.csv"
## [7] "results/notebook_demo/figures/umap_celltypes.png"
pbmc <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "annotate"))
Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type")

knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "tables/annotation_evidence.csv")), digits = 3)

Question: Which clusters need the most careful review before accepting labels?

7. Reactome enrichment

Over-representation compares top positive markers to each cluster’s tested-gene background. BH correction includes all eligible pathways, including zero overlaps. Enrichment does not establish pathway activation or causality.

stage_enrich(cfg)
## [1] "results/notebook_demo/tables/enrichment_all.csv"       
## [2] "results/notebook_demo/tables/enrichment_top.csv"       
## [3] "results/notebook_demo/tables/enrichment_status.json"   
## [4] "results/notebook_demo/objects/enrichment_universes.rds"
## [5] "results/notebook_demo/figures/enrichment.png"
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "figures/enrichment.png")), rel_path = FALSE)

Question: Why would using every human gene as background change the result?

8. Save a report and check raw counts

The report embeds its figures and opens offline. Intermediate RDS objects, full tables, settings and software versions remain available for inspection.

stage_report(cfg)
## [1] "results/notebook_demo/report.html"                    
## [2] "results/notebook_demo/provenance/sessionInfo.txt"     
## [3] "results/notebook_demo/run_summary.json"               
## [4] "results/notebook_demo/provenance/package_versions.csv"
input <- readRDS(object_path(cfg, "ingest"))
expected <- raw_counts(input)[rownames(pbmc), colnames(pbmc), drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(Matrix::nnzero(raw_counts(pbmc) - expected) == 0)
knitr::kable(read.csv(file.path(cfg$output_dir, "provenance/package_versions.csv")))

PBMC3k has one donor and cannot demonstrate a disease/control contrast. The separate DESeq2 extension requires reviewed cell labels and independent donors. See docs/04_multisample.md before adapting it to a real study.
